FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: doujiang
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} soaked overnight, ground with {1_plur} then strained through cloth and brought to the boil — raw, they cannot be digested. Drunk scalding at first light, sweetened with {2_plur} or else salted with vinegar.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: black soy milk
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: black {0_coll} toasted before being ground with {1_plur}, which gives a drink of a violet grey, rounder than yellow soy, lifted with toasted black {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sattu sharbat
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a flour of roasted {0_adj}, slaked in cold {1_plur} with the juice of {2_adj}, black salt and cumin. The drink of the Bihar summers: it feeds as much as it quenches, and needs no cooking at all.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mung bean drink
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: mung {0_coll} cooked past done and passed through a sieve, let down with {1_plur} and scented with fresh {2_plur}. Drunk iced through the heatwaves, for its cooling virtues as much as for its taste.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: po cha
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a brick of {1_adj} boiled for hours with {2_plur}, then churned in a wooden tube with yak {0_coll} and a great deal of salt. It is not an infusion but a fatty broth: at four thousand metres, that is what keeps you upright.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: butter coffee
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a tight {1_coll} let down with hot {2_plur}, into which a knob of {0_adj} is melted and whisked to an emulsion. Without the whisk the fat rises in a pool and the drink is vile.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: buttered grog
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} let down with boiling water over {2_coll} and spices, with a knob of {0_adj} melting on the surface into a shining disc. Served in a tankard, never in a glass: the heat would not hold.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: buttered hot chocolate
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} melted in boiling {2_plur} rather than in milk, and raised with a knob of {0_adj} and a whisk. More bitter and denser than with milk, and this is how it was drunk before the cow got involved.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: coconut water
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a young {0_adj} topped with a machete, whose water is drunk through a straw before the jellied flesh is scraped out with a spoon. Let down with iced {1_plur} and a thread of {2_adj}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: buko shake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the tender flesh of a young {0_adj}, the kind that is scraped out with a spoon, blended with its own water, iced {1_coll} and {2_coll}. In the Philippines it is sold at the roadside in the shell itself.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: coconut and pineapple cooler
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the water and the flesh of a {0_adj} blended with well-ripened {2_coll} and let down with {1_plur}, over a great deal of crushed ice. No cream goes into it: the fruit supplies the richness.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: coconut rum punch
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the water of a {0_adj} poured over {1_coll} and a {2_adj} syrup, served in the shell with a straw. It goes down too easily, which is the whole problem.
